notes: Third-party independently-run leaderboard (DataCurve), not an OpenAI vendor table — do not conflate with the deepswe-v1-1 metric_id (OpenAI's own internal DeepSWE table in openai-gpt-5-6-launch-2026-07.json), hence the distinct metric_id deepswe-leaderboard-datacurve. Harness is mini-swe-agent, NOT Codex's native harness, so these numbers approximate but do not directly measure Codex CLI performance. 113 long-horizon coding tasks, 91 repos, 5 languages. Captured to evaluate the community claim 'Luna at max reasoning effort is the best Codex setting' (see ~/code/dotfiles/ai/research/model-routing/gpt-5-6-luna-at-max-effort-is-a-defensible-not-dominant-codex-value-pick.md): Luna@max is a real cost/quality value point (~92% of Sol@max pass rate at ~7% of Sol@max cost) but is NOT the highest-accuracy point in this table, and confidence intervals across Sol/Terra/Luna@max overlap so the ranking is not statistically decisive at this sample size.

claims.statement: On the DeepSWE third-party leaderboard (mini-swe-agent harness, 113 tasks), gpt-5.6-luna at effort=max reaches ~92% of gpt-5.6-sol@max's pass rate (67% vs 73%) at ~7% of its cost ($0.61 vs $8.39/task); confidence intervals for all three tiers at max overlap.
claims.implication: Luna@max is a real, evidence-backed cost/quality operating point for bounded coding tasks where near-ceiling quality at low cost is acceptable — but it is NOT the highest-accuracy point on this or any table in this catalog, so 'best Codex setting' as an unqualified claim is not supported. Treat as a candidate deescalate-from-Sol operating point, not a universal default.
